chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Where jazz started; the $800 New Orleans script
summary: He does not know where jazz began; at a New Orleans concert he read a script for $800 saying it did.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Would you say that he was responsible for jazz?
No, I wouldn't say nobody was responsible for jazz because I don't know how jazz started.
Did it start in New Orleans?
I don't know. I don't believe it did. I don't know where it started. I don't have the slightest idea.
There was a professor -
That's how people say.
But you don't go along with that theory?
No, but I had to go along that night because I got $800 for saying it.
Where was this?
In New Orleans.
They told you to come down there to play and say something?
...They had a concert down there.
You went along with the idea -
This was where it all originated.
You told them, you're right.
That was my script to read.
Who wrote your script?
I read the script.
Who gave you the script?

The producer. We had a program. We had Sidney Bechet and Louis Armstrong and Jay C. Higginbotham, and the rest they had the house band. You do your solo. They gave you a script to read. That's when they changed - was it Bourbon Street? It was another street. Q: Beale Street?
And changed it back to Beale Street or Bourbon Street. It's been the same street ever since - Bourbon Street.
